title: Loop Check
statement: A treasure hunt has n clues numbered 0 to n − 1. Clue i sends you to clue next[i], or ends the hunt when next[i] is −1. Starting at clue 0, return true if the hunt goes on forever (you reach some clue twice), using O(1) extra space.
constraints: next[i] is −1 or an index from 0 to n − 1

answerKey.pattern: Floyd's cycle detection on a next-index array
keyPoints: Stop with false when fast or next[fast] is −1
Return true when slow equals fast
edgeCases: A long tail before the loop
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Mark visited clues in a set or boolean array: O(n) space

hints: Each clue has exactly one next clue, like a linked list. What tells you it loops?
Run a slow and a fast pointer from clue 0.
If fast reaches −1 the hunt ends; if slow and fast meet, it loops.
